sentences.text: Hesperornis was a large bird measuring between 1.5 and 2 meters in length, though some estimates suggest it could reach up to 1.8 meters.
This animal had virtually no wings and relied on its powerful hind legs to swim.
The genus Hesperornis was formally described and established by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1872.
The first specimen was found in Kansas during Marsh's second expedition to the West in 1871.
Marsh named this initial discovery Hesperornis regalis, a title meaning royal western bird.
This find was one of the lesser-known discoveries made by O. C. Marsh during the late 19th-century Bone Wars.
Studies of limb proportions and hip structure confirm that Hesperornis moved in a manner similar to modern loons or grebes.
Hesperornis legs were likely encased in the body wall up to the ankle, preventing them from standing or walking normally.
Consequently, these birds were likely excellent foot-propelled divers but probably moved ungainly on land.
Hesperornis belongs to the family Hesperornithidae.
Hesperornis lived from the Coniacian to the Maastrichtian, between 89.8 and 66 million years ago.
This marine bird inhabited subtropical to tropical shallow seas like the Western Interior Seaway, the Turgai Strait, and the North Sea.
Youngest specimens found in the freshwater Foremost Formation suggest that some Hesperornis species may have partially abandoned their primarily marine habitat for inland waters.
Recent studies question whether Hesperornis had lobed or webbed toes, with both interpretations considered equally likely.
